subject: Request: IR Playbook + SIG/CAIQ evidence for CardinalPay - follow-up
messages:
From: Anita Shah <security@cardinalpay.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: audit@secureassure.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: IR playbook + SIG/CAIQ evidence following notification

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the heads-up this morning about the authentication anomalies your team notified us about. CardinalPay is conducting a routine post-incident assurance review and we need a few items to complete our vendor SIG/CAIQ mapping and internal risk assessment. Can you provide the following by EOD Thu (48 hours):

- Your current Incident Response Playbook (IRP) — the operational runbook that your on-call will follow for incidents, including escalation contacts and retention timelines.
- SIG/CAIQ evidence pointers for controls related to Identity & Access Management, Logging & Monitoring, and Forensics (specific artifacts or snapshots are fine).
- A short timeline of the observed authentication anomaly (what was detected, when, and the initial containment steps).

If there are known limitations on what you can share (PII, full raw logs), please call that out and provide sanitized samples or hashes we can use for verification. We will share this with our third-party assessor (SecureAssure) and include redaction/handling notes in any export.

Attachment: cardinalpay_questionnaire_SIG_v2.xlsx (their SIG mapping template)

Thanks — we appreciate the quick turnaround. If needed we can extend to next Monday but would prefer sooner.

Best,
Anita Shah
Head of Vendor Security, CardinalPay
security@cardinalpay.com

---
[Attachment stub: cardinalpay_questionnaire_SIG_v2.xlsx]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <security@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IR playbook + SIG/CAIQ evidence following notification

Hi Anita —

Appreciate the note and the template. We're compiling the artifacts now and will aim to deliver a redacted evidence pack by Thursday EOD. Quick notes up-front:

- I've attached our high-level IR summary that outlines roles, escalation tiers, and retention windows (redwood_irp_summary_v1.1.pdf). That should map to the IRP sections in your SIG template.
- For full forensic logs, we can provide a sanitized sample and a checksummed archive; our security team prefers sharing full raw logs over an authenticated SFTP with a signed NDA/POA.
- Timeline below is preliminary; Ben will follow up with forensic detail and log slices.

Preliminary timeline summary:
- 2026-09-14T07:43:12Z — automated monitor flagged elevated failed auths for a subset of service accounts.
- 2026-09-14T07:48:30Z — automatic throttling injected for suspicious IPs; sequences escalated to on-call.
- 2026-09-14T08:05:00Z — ephemeral keys rotated for impacted services; no evidence of token exfiltration at that time.

We will include a short README that maps our artifacts to the SIG/CAIQ control IDs. I will also open a secure upload link and share with your audit contact.

Attaching now: redwood_irp_summary_v1.1.pdf

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Security Partner 
Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IR playbook + SIG/CAIQ evidence following notification

Anita / team —

Following up with the technical artifacts you asked for. Summary and links below.

1) Forensics / Logs:
- We captured relevant auth logs from the API gateway and the identity broker (time window 07:30:00Z–08:15:00Z). Because of PV and customer data safeguards, we are providing a sanitized tarball with request IDs and IPs hashed, plus a redaction map.
- Sample file: forensic_logs_20260914_sample.tar.gz (contains logs and a README with hashes).

2) SIG/CAIQ control mapping:
- I've prepared a short mapping doc that lists where our IRP and monitoring evidence correspond to SIG section 5 (Identity), 8 (Monitoring), and 14 (Forensics). This is in the Drive folder below.

3) Evidence transfer options:
- Preferred: secure SFTP (mutual TLS) with short-lived credentials; we will provide a signed transfer manifest and checksum.
- Alternate: pre-authorized Google Drive share with restricted viewers (we will apply two-person access approval).

Drive folder (access granted to Anita and SecureAssure): https://drive.redwood.example.com/Shared/CardinalPay/IRP-SIG-20260914
Request for audit: please confirm which transfer method you prefer and whether SecureAssure needs their own access ticket.

Attachments included: forensic_logs_20260914_sample.tar.gz

--
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Anita Shah <security@cardinalpay.com>

Cc: audit@secureassure.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IR playbook + SIG/CAIQ evidence following notification

Thanks Ben/Jasmine — this is great and on schedule. A few quick confirmations before our assessor reviews: 

- SecureAssure will take the SFTP route. They require an audit token and a short Service Account manifest (we will send their request ID once they accept the folder).
- Can you include a brief statement of scope (one paragraph) that we can attach to our SIG submission describing what was redacted and why (PII, customer-identifiable fields, etc.)?
- Please include retention/restore windows for the provided artifacts (how long they will be available on SFTP/Drive before automatic removal).

If you can get the SFTP creds and the scope paragraph to us tomorrow morning, SecureAssure will begin their verification and we should close this out by end of next week. Appreciate the quick collaboration.

Best regards,
Anita Shah
Head of Vendor Security, CardinalPay
security@cardinalpay.com
